absent: Dirty ring allocation, capacity negotiation, reset harvesting and userspace memory layout.
Slot dirty tracking enablement lifecycle and bitmap allocation and teardown.
Synchronization for synthetic debugging control block shared across virtual processors.
Synthetic controller activation, version negotiation and event and message page setup.
Construction, update and invalidation of the cached APIC destination map.
Vendor specific delivery hook behavior and end of interrupt completion.
Timestamp page establishment, state transitions and clock accuracy.
Scheduling request and kick mechanics for exit, event and injected interrupts.

findings.text: A helper records that a guest frame became dirty inside a memory slot. Callers supply the virtual machine, the slot descriptor and the guest frame number. The operation has no result and tolerates a missing slot by doing nothing further.

Dirty accounting occurs only when a slot is present and its tracking flag is active. The position stored is relative to the start of the slot rather than absolute. The slot identity combines address space and slot number into one value, with the space occupying the upper portion.

When a per virtual machine ring capacity is configured and a running virtual processor is available, dirty reports go to that processor ring. Otherwise, when a slot level bitmap exists, the corresponding bit is marked. If neither path is available, the call has no visible effect beyond validation.
Recording dirtiness without a running virtual processor is unexpected when the virtual machine still has users. The generic permission hook denies such writes, so the path warns and aborts.

A global accessor returns the virtual processor currently executing on this physical processor, or a null indicator when none is running. Preemption is briefly suppressed around the per processor read to keep the observed value stable.

The running processor lookup relies on preemption control rather than an explicit spinlock. Disabling preemption pins the caller while fetching the per processor current value, then reenables scheduling.

Each virtual processor owns a dirty queue with a fixed capacity, a producer position, a consumer reset position, a soft threshold and an array of entries. Each entry carries a combined slot identity, a slot relative offset and a flag word that marks the entry as containing valid dirtiness.

Publishing a dirty entry writes identity and offset first, issues an ordering barrier, then sets the valid marker and finally advances the producer position. Userspace is the intended consumer and no kernel reader is paired, so the barrier only orders against that external observer.

Occupancy is the difference between producer and consumer positions observed with single load accessors. The queue counts as full when occupancy reaches capacity and as softly full when occupancy reaches the configured soft threshold. The target slot is chosen by masking the producer position with capacity minus one, which implies capacity is a power of two.

Pushing while the queue is already full is treated as a programming error that warns but still proceeds. Reaching the soft threshold raises a scheduling request on the same virtual processor so that userspace harvesting can be expedited.

Synthetic debugging availability is decided by inspecting a cached capability word for the kernel debugging allowance bit. The check is read only and gates both host initiated and guest initiated accesses differently.

Synthetic debugging state lives once per virtual machine under the Hyper-V extension, not per virtual processor. It holds a control block with control and status plus send, receive and pending page descriptors, alongside a separate options field.

Writes and reads to the synthetic debugging register group update or return the matching stored field and report success. Control and pending buffer writes from the guest additionally divert to userspace for external handling, while host writes complete inline. Status, send, receive and options accesses never divert.

When the debugging capability is absent, guest accesses to the debugging registers fail with a nonzero indication while host accesses still succeed. Unknown register numbers inside the handler are ignored and still report success.

A guest write that requires external assistance fills a Hyper-V exit descriptor with the register identity and snapshots of control and page fields, installs a completion callback on the virtual processor and raises an exit request. Completion copies back only the status value when the originating register was the control register.

Synthetic interrupt controller registers are read through a per controller helper that maps control, version, event page, message page, end of interrupt and sixteen synthetic lines to stored values. End of interrupt always reads as zero and each line value is fetched atomically.

Reads from an inactive controller fail for guest callers but succeed for host callers. Unrecognized register numbers also fail, distinguishing them from the debugging register group which ignores unknowns.

Delivering a synthetic line interrupt validates kernel interrupt controller presence and line range, resolves the programmed vector and drops the request when no vector is armed. Otherwise a fixed self directed physical edge request is built and handed to the local interrupt delivery path.

Interrupt delivery is offered as a thin wrapper that forwards to a full delivery routine with no additional timekeeping context. The full routine first attempts an accelerated path and otherwise scans all virtual processors for matching destinations.
Injection into a single virtual processor resolves its local interrupt object and forwards delivery mode, vector, level and trigger details to the acceptance routine.

Acceptance branches on delivery mode. Fixed and lowest priority share edge and enable checks before invoking the vendor delivery hook. Remote read wakes the target, management and nonmaskable modes inject the corresponding event and kick, init arms a pending init flag, startup latches a vector with ordering before arming pending startup, and external is intentionally ignored.

Fixed delivery discards level deassertions for edge triggered semantics and discards everything when the controller is software or hardware disabled. Trigger mode memory is synchronized to match the incoming trigger before delivery, and an optional timekeeping map can record the affected processor and vector.

A controller counts as enabled only when both software and hardware indications agree. Each indication consults a global disable switch first and falls back to per object state when that switch is active. Presence additionally requires in kernel emulation.

System management interrupts are injectable only when the emulated base register is advertised. One build always reports unavailability. Successful injection raises a dedicated request. Nonmaskable injection unconditionally increments a queued counter and raises its own request.

Destination matching first normalizes the identifier through a quirk helper, then honors shorthand. No shorthand consults physical or logical matchers according to mode, self matches only the source object, all inclusive always matches, all exclusive matches everything except the source, and unknown shorthands never match.

Physical matching accepts broadcast identifiers immediately. Extended mode or identifiers too large for legacy encoding compare against the numeric virtual processor identity, while legacy mode compares against the identifier register shifted down from its storage position.

Logical matching also accepts broadcast first. Extended mode requires cluster overlap in the upper portion plus nonzero overlap in the lower portion. Legacy flat mode requires any overlap of identifiers, legacy cluster mode requires matching cluster nibbles plus overlap within the cluster, and unknown formats never match.

Identity sources include a per processor numeric identifier used for extended mode, a register backed legacy identifier extracted from the high byte of its register, a mode bit taken from the base register and a generic register reader that indexes the memory mapped register file.

The destination normalizer rewrites legacy broadcast to extended broadcast when the quirk is enabled, the request did not originate from a local controller and the target runs in extended mode. All other identifiers pass through unchanged.

Lowest priority handling applies when the delivery mode selects it or when a message signaled hint asks for redirection. Priority comparison subtracts arbitration counters, with a negative outcome meaning the first candidate outranks the second.
Hashed delivery picks the nth set bit where n is the vector modulo the number of eligible destinations. Selecting beyond the bitmap size is treated as a fatal programming error.

The accelerated delivery path handles self delivery without consulting shared tables. Other destinations are resolved under a read side critical section that protects the shared destination map, then each resolved target is injected in turn.

Map based resolution rejects non self shorthands, missing maps and broadcast destinations. Physical mode indexes the flat table with speculation hardening and tolerates out of range identifiers as empty. Logical mode delegates to a format specific helper and, for lowest priority, either scans for minimal arbitration value or uses hashed selection with disabled target detection.

The cached map supports disabled, extended, flat and cluster logical organizations. Disabled software mode yields an empty mask, extended mode slices the physical table by high identifier portion with clamped cluster width, flat mode masks the low byte, and cluster mode selects a table by middle nibble and masks the low nibble.

Whether an identifier counts as broadcast depends on a quirk flag. With the quirk disabled, legacy and extended broadcasts are recognized according to the current logical organization. With the quirk enabled, only the broadcast matching the source mode counts.
Encountering a disabled target during hashed selection records a sticky per virtual machine flag and emits a one time informational message. Later encounters remain silent.

The slow delivery path clears a per invocation destination bitmap, iterates all virtual processors skipping absent controllers and nonmatching destinations, injects directly for non lowest priority modes while accumulating a success count, and defers lowest priority to either minimal arbitration or hashed bitmap selection before a single injection.
A physical broadcast combined with lowest priority is demoted to fixed delivery with an informational notice, avoiding undefined arbitration across all processors.

Routing entries for synthetic lines ignore deassertions and fail when the target processor has no controller. End of interrupt handling acknowledges every line currently programmed to the retiring vector. A global refresh walks the routing table and caches the global interrupt number inside each addressed line object.

The routing refresh observes the routing table through a sleepable read side accessor that requires the interrupt lock to be held, then iterates every global entry and filters for synthetic line types.

The reference counter returns scaled kernel clock when the shared timestamp page is not in the ready state. Otherwise it reads the first virtual processor timestamp, applies guest scaling and then applies a second scale plus offset from the Hyper-V timestamp configuration.

Guest timestamp construction adds a per processor offset to the host value after optional ratio scaling. Ratio scaling is skipped entirely when the configured ratio equals the system default, otherwise a fixed point multiply with configured fractional width is used.
The synthetic controller exposes sixteen line registers numbered consecutively from zero. This width governs validation of line indices and sizing of per line state.

Local interrupt delivery distinguishes fixed, lowest priority, management, nonmaskable, init, startup, remote read, external and shorthand based targeting with physical versus logical destination modes.
A dedicated flag value marks a dirty ring entry as containing valid dirtiness. Software sets this marker after filling identity and offset and before advancing the producer position.

Synthetic debugging uses six registers covering control, status, send buffer, receive buffer, pending buffer and options. Control and pending writes can divert to userspace while the others complete in kernel.
